root_cause_label: Superficial Disassembly Read and Partial Output Verification
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent only read the first 50 lines of main's disassembly, missing the sphere positions and checkered-floor parameters, then wrote guessed ray-tracer code and repeatedly verified only the background-pixel header rows where its output happened to match, never detecting the missing geometry.
t_err_evidence: Step 7 uses 'grep -A 50 <main>:' to read only the first 50 lines of main's disassembly. This is far too shallow for a path tracer that encodes scene geometry (sphere positions, floor pattern) in floating-point constants deeper in the function. The agent then (step 8) incorrectly infers 'fractal generation like Mandelbrot or Julia' and later a single generic sphere, having never seen the actual scene constants.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11 writes the full C implementation as a generic single-sphere ray marcher with guessed camera and lighting parameters (ray_origin={0,0,-4}, radius=1, light_dir={0.5,-0.5,-0.5}), without returning to the disassembly. All subsequent steps merely tweak lighting constants within this same wrong framework, locking in the missing-geometry failure.
t_surface_evidence: Step 16 shows the comparison: reversed.ppm starts with all '159 197 255' (pure background), while image.ppm shifts to '158 197 255' just after the header — a minor but observable discrepancy in even the background gradient. More critically, a deeper comparison would reveal completely different foreground (sphere, checkered floor) which the agent's head-only check never reaches.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that reading 50 lines of main's disassembly was sufficient to understand the scene. It then assumed the algorithm was 'fractal generation' from the generic floating-point instructions it saw, without extracting the actual scene geometry constants embedded further in the binary.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10 shows reversed.ppm starts with '0 0 0' pixels while image.ppm starts with '159 197 255' — the agent acknowledges this but dismisses it as expected since 'the fractal nature means any algorithm difference will create a wildly different image anyway'. Step 13 shows reversed.ppm output still stuck at '0 0 0' pixels, a clear signal the implementation is wrong.
